sections.h2: Where is the Cocke County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Cocke County Register of Deeds sits in the courthouse at 111 Court Avenue in Newport, Tennessee 37821. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:30, and the office also opens Saturday from 8:00 to 11:00.

The office phone is (423) 623-7540, the fax line is (423) 623-7556, and the email address is ccrod@cockecountytn.gov. Mark McGaha holds the office and has worked there since September 2010. He took over in December 2016, when the county legislative body appointed him after Linda Benson retired.

The Newport courthouse is the one place where a Cocke County deed becomes part of the public record. If you are selling a house here, the closing agent normally brings the signed deed to this counter, but you can also walk a document in yourself during the hours above. The county's Register of Deeds page carries the current staff list and fee schedule.

sections.h2: Which fees apply when a Cocke County deed gets recorded?
sections.html:
A warranty deed or quitclaim deed costs $5.00 per page, with a $10.00 minimum charge and a $2.00 data processing fee. The same per-page rate applies to deeds of trust, leases, liens, judgments, restrictions, agreements and amendments.

The county fee page says its figures follow Tennessee Code 8-21-1001. Other items on that schedule are priced differently:

  • Releases of a single lien run $10.00 for one or two pages plus the $2.00 data processing fee, then $5.00 for each added page and $5.00 for each added deed reference.
  • Assignments and modifications are $10.00 for one or two pages with one assignment, plus $2.00, with $5.00 for every extra page or deed reference.
  • Financing statements filed as a fixture filing cost $15.00, and each extra party indexed adds $15.00. A husband and wife count as two names for that indexing.
  • Charters cost $5.00 for up to five pages plus $2.00, and 50 cents for each page after that.
  • Certified copies are $1.00 plus $1.00 per page.

Every document except releases and charters has to show the name and address of the person or company that prepared it. An assignment or modification must also carry a statement of the maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes, even when that figure is $0.

sections.h2: How much is the state transfer tax on a Cocke County sale?
sections.html:
The register collects the state tax at $3.70 per $1,000, which is 37 cents per $100. The Tennessee Department of Revenue says this realty transfer tax applies to all transfers of realty and is generally based on the greater of the price paid or the value of the property.

On a $158,000 sale, for example, the tax would come to about $585, since 1,580 units of $100 times $0.37 gives $584.60. Cocke County's own page lists a $1.00 probate fee that is collected only when state tax is paid.

A new mortgage or deed of trust carries a separate indebtedness tax. The county page lists it at $1.15 per $1,000 with the first $2,000 exempt, and the state revenue help page gives the same rate as $0.115 per $100. The statute behind both taxes is Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409.

sections.h2: What can the Cocke County register staff do for you, and what can they not?
sections.html:
Staff will record, index and copy documents, but they will not write a deed for you. The office states that it may not prepare documents or perform title searches because staff are neither bonded nor licensed attorneys.

That matters for an owner who inherited a house or is selling without an agent. A title company, a real estate attorney or a closing agent drafts the deed and checks the chain of title. The register receives the finished instrument and charges the fees listed above.

The register has also set up a fraud alert system. You enter a first and last name and an email address on the website the county links to, and you get an email any time a document is recorded under that name. Owners of a house they plan to sell, or of land they do not live on, can use it to spot a forged deed early.

sections.h2: What is Cocke County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Cocke County is a rural, mountainous county on Tennessee's eastern edge, and its sale prices sit well below the state's cities. The county has about 37,889 residents by the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, up 5.3% from the April 2020 count of 35,999.

sections.h2: Which towns and landscape shape property in Cocke County?
sections.html:
Newport is the county seat and the largest city. Parrottsville is the other incorporated town, and Cosby is a census-designated place. The county covers 443 square miles, and the Census lists 436 of them as land.

The southern part of Cocke County lies in the Great Smoky Mountains, and the northern part is Ridge-and-Valley terrain. The French Broad River crosses the north, and part of it forms Douglas Lake. English Mountain dominates the western side. Interstate 40, US 25, US 70 and US 321 give road access, and parts of Cherokee National Forest, the Appalachian Trail and Great Smoky Mountains National Park fall inside the county line.

The state created the county on October 9, 1797, from part of Greene County, and named it for Senator William Cocke. For a seller, the terrain means the legal description in a deed deserves a close read. Ask your closing agent to confirm it matches the parcel before recording.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a house you sell in Cocke County?
sections.html:
County taxes on Tennessee real estate become due the first Monday in October and are delinquent after the last day of February, according to the state Comptroller's assessment schedule. The year's assessment date is January 1.

The Cocke County Register of Deeds does not collect property tax, and its records do not show what is owed. Ask the Cocke County Trustee for a payoff on the parcel before closing, and ask the County Assessor of Property about the appraised value and classification. A title company will request the same figures when it prepares the settlement statement.

If you plan to dispute a value, the state schedule says the general deadline for an appeal to the State Board of Equalization is August 1, or 45 days after the county board's notice goes out, whichever is later.

sections.h2: What should you bring to the register's counter?
sections.html:
Bring the original signed and notarized deed, the names and addresses of the buyer and seller, the preparer's name and address, and payment for fees and tax. Check with the office on how it takes payment before you go.

  • The deed itself, with the preparer's name and address printed on it.
  • The sale price or value, so the state transfer tax can be computed.
  • A check or other payment covering the per-page fee, the $2.00 data processing fee and the $3.70 per $1,000 tax.
  • For a release, the lien details and the deed book reference, since each added reference costs $5.00.

Call (423) 623-7540 or email the office if your document is unusual and you want to confirm the fees before you drive to Newport.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Cocke County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $5.00 per page with a $10.00 minimum and a $2.00 data processing fee. A three-page warranty deed would therefore be $15.00 plus $2.00, or $17.00, before any state tax. The Register of Deeds page on the county website carries the full schedule.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Cocke County house sale?
faqs.a: The state tax is $3.70 per $1,000, or 37 cents per $100, based generally on the greater of the price or the property value. A $200,000 sale would owe $740. The county lists it as state tax, and the Department of Revenue cites Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409.

faqs.q: Can the Cocke County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says it may not prepare documents or perform title searches because staff are neither bonded nor licensed attorneys. A title company or attorney writes the deed, and the register records it once it meets the preparer-name rule.

faqs.q: Is the Cocke County Register of Deeds open on Saturday?
faqs.a: Yes, on Saturday mornings from 8:00 to 11:00. Monday through Friday the office keeps hours from 8:00 to 4:30. The phone number is (423) 623-7540, and the courthouse address is 111 Court Avenue in Newport.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether anyone recorded a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Sign up for the register's fraud alert. You enter your name and an email address on the website the county links to, and the system emails you whenever a document is recorded under that name. You can also call the office to ask about a specific filing.
